title: Plan the text in layers
statement: Plan each text in layers before writing it: what it states, what it implies with support, and plausible neighbouring ideas it does not support, kept for the wrong options.
detail: In a Grade 3 demonstration unit, passages carry a header that plans their layers before the text: what is stated and what is implied with support, and for the unseen capstone passage also plausible neighbouring ideas the text does not support, listed for use as distractors. A primer passage's header lists its stated and implied layers, including one implied point the text raises but does not settle.
against: Planning layers did not by itself make items need the text: none of the 10 selected-response items written on the capstone passage passed its anti-leak gate, 8 of them answerable without any passage and 2 from the taught texts alone (`grade3-reading/artifacts/demo-unit-2026-07-10/phase-e/capstone/gate-capstone-summary.json`, lines 12-16).

evidence.quote: unsupported-plausible neighbors (for distractors; NOT in the text)
layers: stated = photo figure, both jar results, current definition, muddy-means-carrying; implied = high water carries more than low water
